title: Make 10 and 20
goal: I can find the missing partner in a bond to 10 and to 20. I can tell when the 2 sides are equal.

learn.intro: A number bond is 2 numbers that make a whole. 6 and 4 make 10. So 6 + 4 = 10 and 10 = 6 + 4. Bonds to 10 help us find bonds to 20.

example.problem: Aisha has 20 beads. 14 beads are blue and the rest are white. How many beads are white?
steps: The whole is 20. One part is 14. We want the other part.
14 is 10 and 4 more. We need 4 and some more to make 10: 4 + 6 = 10.

howto.title: How to find the missing partner
steps: Look at the ones digit of the part you know. What makes 10 with it?
Add the partners. Do they make the whole?

try.explanation: 7 and 3 make 10, so 17 and 3 make 20. Check: 17 + 3 = 20.

items.text: Look at the ten-frame.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many more counters fill the frame? {b} counters

items.explanation: The frame has 10 spaces. 4 are full, so 6 are empty. 4 + 6 = 10.

items.text: Fill in the missing numbers.
items.explanation: Think of the partner that makes 10: 8 and 2, 7 and 3, 5 and 5, 1 and 9.

items.text: Kumar has 10 marbles. 6 marbles are in his pocket. The rest are in a bag. How many marbles are in the bag? {b} marbles
items.explanation: 6 and 4 make 10, so 4 marbles are in the bag.

items.text:
Write the partner that makes 10.
1 and {b}     3 and {b}     6 and {b}     8 and {b}
Write the missing number in each bond.
items.explanation: First bond: 12 = 7 + 5. Second bond: the two parts 6 and 8 make 14.

items.text: Fill in the missing numbers.
items.hint: Look at the ones digit. What makes 10 with it?

items.text:
7 + 3 = 10. Use it to fill in the blanks.
17 + {b} = 20     27 + {b} = 30     47 + {b} = 50
items.explanation: The ones digit is 7 each time. 7 + 3 = 10, so each number needs 3 more to reach the next ten.

items.text: Mei has a shelf for 20 books. There are 16 books on the shelf. How many more books fit? {b} books
Fill in the missing number. Both sides must be equal.
items.explanation: The sign = means both sides have the same value. 6 + 5 = 11, and 7 + 4 = 11. 8 + 2 = 10, and 5 + 5 = 10. 9 + 4 = 13, and 8 + 5 = 13.

items.text: Look at the pairs that make 9.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The first numbers go up by 1. The second numbers go {circ:up|down} by 1.

items.explanation: 2 + 7, 3 + 6 and 4 + 5 all make 9. When one number goes up by 1, the other goes down by 1, so the total stays 9.

items.text: Circle True or False.
items.explanation: 8 + 3 = 11, not 10. 15 + 6 = 21, not 20. The other two are correct bonds.

items.text: There are 20 children in a club. 7 children are girls. The rest are boys. How many boys are in the club? {b} boys
items.explanation: 7 + 3 = 10, so 7 + 13 = 20. There are 13 boys.

items.text: Kumar has 8 stickers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: He wants 10 stickers. How many more does he need? {b} stickers

parts.label: b
parts.text: He wants 20 stickers. How many more does he need? {b} stickers

items.text: Ravi puts 14 marbles into 2 bags. The first bag has fewer marbles than the second bag. Each bag has at least 1 marble. Write every way in the table.
items.hint: Try 1 marble in the first bag. Then 2. Where do you stop?
items.explanation: The ways are 1 and 13, 2 and 12, 3 and 11, 4 and 10, 5 and 9, 6 and 8. 7 and 7 is not allowed because the first bag must have fewer.

items.text: Each shape stands for a number. The same shape is always the same number.
items.hint: Cover the 5. What do the 2 stars make together?
items.explanation: (a) 17 - 5 = 12, and 6 + 6 = 12, so ★ = 6. (b) Three equal numbers make 21: 7 + 7 + 7 = 21, so ● = 7.

items.text: Three different numbers from 1 to 6 add up to 9. Find every set of three.
items.hint: Write each set from smallest to greatest. Start with 1.
items.explanation: With 1 as the smallest: 1 + 2 + 6 and 1 + 3 + 5. With 2 as the smallest: 2 + 3 + 4. The smallest number cannot be 3 or more, because 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.

items.text: Ali has 16 stickers. Mei has 8 stickers. Ali gives some of his stickers to Mei. Now each child has an equal number of stickers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many stickers does Ali give Mei? {b} stickers

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many stickers does each child have now? {b} stickers

items.hint: How many stickers are there in all? What would be fair?
items.explanation: 16 + 8 = 24 stickers. Shared equally, each child has 12. Ali goes from 16 to 12, so he gives 4.

items.text: Mei puts 17 sweets in 2 jars. Jar A has 5 more sweets than Jar B.
items.hint: Imagine Jar A without its 5 extra sweets.
items.explanation: 17 - 5 = 12. Shared equally, each jar gets 6. Jar A also has the 5 extra: 6 + 5 = 11. Check: 11 + 6 = 17.

items.text: I am a number. When I add 7, the answer ends in 0 and is between 15 and 45. What can I be? Find them all.
items.hint: Which numbers between 15 and 45 end in 0?
items.explanation: The numbers that end in 0 between 15 and 45 are 20, 30 and 40. Take away 7 from each: 13, 23 and 33.

items.text: Pick 2 different numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and add them.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write every total you can make. Begin with the smallest. {ll}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which totals can you make in only one way? {ll}

items.hint: List the pairs in order. Start with 1 + 2.
items.explanation: The pairs are 1+2=3, 1+3=4, 1+4=5, 1+5=6, 2+3=5, 2+4=6, 2+5=7, 3+4=7, 3+5=8, 4+5=9. The totals are 3 to 9. 5, 6 and 7 can each be made two ways. 3, 4, 8 and 9 only one way.
2 and 8 make 10.
6 and 4 make 10, so 6 and 14 make 20.

items.text: There are 20 flowers. 11 are red. The rest are yellow. How many flowers are yellow? {b} flowers
